author: addisondunn
body: ## Product Description Using the Linked project spaces (LINKED_DOMAINS) feature flag, the Linked Project Spaces feature allows enterprise projects with multiple domains to push content from an upstream domain to a downstream domain: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6729291/138953370-353c8fa7-6a79-4ca0-8027-d47031387e3c.png) This PR adds Automatic Update Rules as a type of content that can be pushed to a downstream domain. ~~Similar to how the other types of content work, upon push *all* rules with all of their details will be pushed and overwrite all of the rules on the downstream domain. It does not add the rules, it will "sync and overwrite".~~ Existing rules in the downstream linked domain will not be deleted. But if a rule in the downstream domain has the same name, _it will be overwritten_. The rule name, case type, and all of the criteria and actions for a rule are copied over in their exact form and vocabulary to the downstream domain. ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6729291/138953506-1369a17a-9ffa-4817-a240-c734e339c6fd.png) Note that inactive rules will be copied as well. And as with all linked domain content, an email will be sent to the user once the rules have been copied over successfully. ## Technical Summary In response to [USH-561](https://dimagi-dev.atlassian.net/browse/USH-561?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjMxOWZiMTIxMWIxNDJjMTkxOWViYWU0ODE1MGVhZmEiLCJwIjoiaiJ9). This PR followed [Jenny's PR to add lookup tables](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-hq/pull/27855) and [Steph's PR to add certain settings](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-hq/pull/28525) to linked project space content. You'll see the commits are similar step-by-step. ~~And like some of the other update methods, I _deleted all_ of the automatic update rules in the downstream domain and then copied them over.~~ Downstream rules are given an upstream ID to mark the rule they are connected to in the upstream domain. The local accessor method felt a bit verbose, but there really seemed no easier way than to serialize the models associated with automatic update rules (CaseRuleCriteria and CaseRuleAction and their definitions) field-by-field. Note that the AutomaticUpdateRule model has two different workflow types: CASE_UPDATE and SCHEDULING. The former is the only one used in this PR because the latter is used, from what I can tell, only to set schedules for messaging (in the ScheduleInstance model, for Conditional Alerts). From my exploration of the codebase, no other models use AutomaticUpdateRule primary keys. If that were true, deleting all the rules for the downstream domain and recreating the way I do here would be bad news (ScheduleInstance models, for example, rely on AutomaticUpdateRule primary IDs). ## Feature Flag Linked project spaces (LINKED_DOMAINS) ## Safety Assurance ### Safety story Locally, I tested pushing automatic update rules to downstream domains with many different kinds of criteria and actions. I also tested to make sure inactive rules are pushed as well. On staging I will be testing that the email is sent to the user to confirm that the rules have been copied. I will also make sure that a copied rule is working properly locally and on staging. ### Automated test coverage I wrote a test in test_update_auto_update_rules.py that 1) creates a set of rules 2) copies them over using the update method, and then 3) tests to make sure those rules look the same in the new domain. The test passed. ### QA Plan ~~None right now (following the guidance from the tech sprint google sheet), unless something thinks that should change.~~ QA will be pulled in. ### Migrations There is one migration to add an upstream_id field to the AuotmaticUpdateRule model so that we can track which rules in the downstream domain are linked to upstream rules when pushing content. - [x] Migrations can be reverted after deploy ### Rollback instructions - [x] This PR can be reverted after deploy with no further considerations ### Labels & Review - [x] Risk label is set correctly - [x] The set of people pinged as reviewers is appropriate for the level of risk of the change

author: spalger
body:
The `x-pack/test/apm_api_integration` configs use a custom "registry" object to manage which tests run for different Kibana configs. This object currently uses mutable variables in module scope to keep track of tests, a pattern which has all sorts of problems and should be avoided. A recent tweak to the way that tests are run/loaded caused these variables to break and prevent APM tests from running when they should be.

The fix I've implemented here is moving away from these mutable variables in module scope and converting `registry` to a service, which is recreated for each execution of the tests.

This required adding a new FTR config option: `servicesRequiredForTestAnalysis`. This option contains an array of service names which won't be mocked out for test analysis, a process used to prevent services from accidentally initializing state or causing side effects when we're just analyzing the tests. Since this service (and it's config dependency) are necessary for defining tests they are "required for test analysis" and are added to that config.

Unhides and re-enables the test button in Javalab now that Javabuilder supports running tests (behind an experiment flag, `"javalabUnitTests"`). This turned out to be a little more involved than just hooking up the existing test function to the test button - there was some additional work required to ensure that Run and Test couldn't be called at the same time.

I also added a [tech debt task](https://codedotorg.atlassian.net/browse/CSA-1025) to the backlog to ensure that Javalab never has more than one Javabuilder execution at a time; in theory, this shouldn't happen as the logic here should prevent you from clicking Run while tests are in progress and vice versa, and even if it does, each lambda should provide an isolated environment per execution. Still though, it might be good to have an additional layer of security to prevent unintended consequences especially as we add new use cases for connecting to Javabuilder (e.g. compile only for backpack).

You may want to ignore files that contain sensitive credentials or information which should not be pushed to your repository. There are a few ways to tell Git which files to ignore. ### Ignoring files Git uses a file called `.gitignore` to decide which files and directories to ignore when committing. Keep files containing sensitive data, like configuration or `env` files, out of your repositories. This is one way to promote security best practices. The `.gitignore` file can, and should, be committed into your repository. By sharing this file and making it part of your code, it will also help others. Other users that contribute to the repository will also avoid committing sensitive data. There are many examples of `.gitignore` files available for you to use in your own repositories. author: chrisr3
body:
The CPKs are typically installed into a JUnit `@TempDir` directory, which JUnit deletes once the test is complete. However, Windows cannot delete either an open file or a non-empty directory, and so all these CPK objects must be closed before JUnit tries to delete the temporary directory that contains them.

Add an `@AfterAll` method to shut the `InstallService` down, so that it can close all of its CPK instances. This should then allow Windows to remove the temporary directory.

And am I the only person who thinks that `ServiceLocator` (with its "static" functions) is an anti-pattern?

body:
## Goal

This is the baseline for building common derivers from clientAPI and v3 with normalization across all data sources.

## To Do:

- [x] Add a common deriver
- [x] Document common deriver
- [x] Add Tests

Collection
- [x] page.spec.js
- [x] story.spec.js

Discover
- [x] discover.spec.js

List
- [x] collection.spec.js
- [x] image.spec.js
- [x] video.spec.js
- [x] legacy.spec.js
- [x] parsed.spec.js
- [x] unparsed.spec.js


## Implementation Decisions

We use a common card to display data but our derivers were all over the place.  This moves all derivers to a central place and creates some normalization and predictability about what item data will be available.

## Derived URLs
A key element of this is to simplify the urls we pass with the derived item.

URLS to use
- externalUrl — open original action from the publisher link with added UTM
- readUrl — item action when the user clicks on the image or title of a saved item
- saveUrl — the url to use when an item is to be saved from a save action
- permanentUrl — url for Pockets internal library [premium feature]
- analyticsUrl — this is included in the analyticsData payload to avoid confusion

openUrl will be derived from external/read urls based on the existence of a readUrl (which will only exists if the item has been saved and parsed)

---

## Note

None of this is used in production yet. This is solely set up work to better make the transition between v3 and clientApi

There will be a follow up PR that will go over the anatomy of a card and how this data connects to it
